name: notebook_edit
description: Edit one cell of a Jupyter notebook (.ipynb) by cell number, as shown by read_file. Use this rather than edit_file/write_file for notebooks: it edits the cell's source directly instead of the JSON-escaped text inside the document, and leaves other cells, their outputs, and notebook metadata untouched. Replacing a code cell clears its stale outputs. Cell numbers are 1-based.

path.description: Path to the .ipynb file, relative to the project root.

cell.description: Which cell (1-based), as numbered by read_file. For insert, the new cell takes this position, so one past the last cell appends.

mode.description: Replace the cell's source (default), insert a new cell at this position, or delete the cell.

source.description: The cell's new source, as plain text. Required for replace and insert.

cell_type.description: Cell kind. For insert, defaults to the kind of the cell currently at this position. For replace, pass it only to convert the cell to a different kind.

name: ast_grep
description: Structural (AST-aware) code search using ast-grep. Matches code by syntax-tree shape rather than text, so it ignores formatting/whitespace and supports meta-variables: $NAME matches one node, $$$ARGS matches a list. Examples: "console.log($A)", "function $F($$$) { $$$ }", "useEffect($CB, [])". Returns matching "path:line:col: text" entries. Prefer this over search_files when you want occurrences of a code *pattern* (calls, declarations, JSX elements) without regex false positives. Requires the language of the code.

pattern.description: An ast-grep structural pattern, e.g. "console.log($A)" or "function $F($$$) { $$$ }".

lang.description: Language of the pattern/files: ts, tsx, js, jsx, py, rust, go, java, c, cpp, ruby, etc.

path.description: Subdirectory to search within (default project root).

name: view_localhost
description: Load a localhost/loopback URL (e.g. a dev server you started with run_shell) in a headless browser, take a screenshot, and capture the page's visible text and console output. The screenshot is returned as an image you can view directly, so you can see the web UI you built and iterate on it instead of guessing. Pass steps to exercise a flow before the screenshot (fill a login form, click submit, wait for the next page): each step's result is reported, the run stops at the first failing step, and the screenshot shows where it ended. Judge whether a flow worked with expect_text steps or the returned page text, not from the screenshot alone. Every call is a fresh page load: typed input and other in-page state from an earlier call are gone (cookies and localStorage persist), so put a whole flow in one call's steps. Use test data, not the user's real credentials. Pass variants to capture the page in several viewports or color schemes at once (desktop, tablet, or mobile presets, light or dark, full page); the user sees them as a gallery labelled as the running app. Steps run with at most one variant. Only loopback hosts (localhost, 127.0.0.1, ::1) are allowed; use web_fetch for public URLs. This is local network egress, so it always requires approval, and calls with steps are approved separately from plain views.

url.description: A loopback URL to load, e.g. "http://localhost:3000".

selector.description: Optional CSS selector: screenshot just that element's bounding box instead of the whole viewport (e.g. "#app", ".hero").

variants.description: Optional viewports to capture, each from a fresh page load (at most 6). Without it, one 1280×800 capture in the OS color scheme.

preset.description: Viewport preset: desktop 1280×800, tablet 768×1024, mobile 390×844. Defaults to desktop.

label.description: Short name shown under the image, e.g. "Mobile, dark".

width.description: Custom viewport width in CSS pixels (200 to 2560).

height.description: Custom viewport height in CSS pixels (200 to 2000).

fullPage.description: Capture the whole page height (up to 6000px).

steps.description: Optional interactions run in order after the page loads and before the screenshot (at most 20). fill sets an input, textarea, or select value and leaves it focused; click clicks an element and waits for any page load it starts; dblclick double-clicks an element; press presses a key on the selector's element, or on the focused element when selector is omitted; wait_for waits until a selector matches a visible element (timeout_ms, default and max 10000); expect_text passes once value appears in the visible text of the page, or of an element matching selector (case-insensitive; form field values are not visible text), or with absent: true once it does not, failing after timeout_ms (default 3000, max 10000); wait pauses (ms, max 5000).

selector.description: Standard CSS selector, no :contains() or :has-text() (fill, click, dblclick, wait_for; optional for press and expect_text).

value.description: Text to enter (fill), or the text to look for (expect_text).

absent.description: expect_text: pass only when the text is not visible.

timeout_ms.description: How long wait_for or expect_text waits.

name: show_images
description: Show image files to the user, each with a short label and an optional caption: as a gallery they can open full size in the desktop app, or as clickable file links in the terminal. Use it to present screenshots or renders you produced (for example of a UI before and after a change, or a page in light and dark themes) instead of describing them in words. Files must be PNG, JPEG, GIF, or WebP inside the project, at most 5 MB each. You also receive the images, so look at them before you describe them. Say in your reply which images come from the running app and which are mockups.

title.description: Optional heading for the gallery, e.g. "Settings page: proposed".

images.description: The images to show, in order (1 to 12).

path.description: Path to the image file, relative to the project root.

label.description: Short name shown under the image, e.g. "Dark theme". Defaults to the file name.

caption.description: Optional sentence shown with the image in the full-size viewer.

compareWith.description: Optional path to another image to compare this one against, such as the same screen before a change; the viewer shows the two with a slider.

name: render_mockup
description: Render an HTML mockup file from the project into screenshots, with no dev server, and show them to the user as a gallery. Use it to show how a UI that doesn't exist yet would look: write a self-contained .html page that uses the project's own stylesheet and theme tokens, then render it in the states that matter. The page can load files from its own project folder (CSS, fonts, images, scripts) but nothing from the network. Each variant picks a viewport preset (desktop, tablet, mobile) or a custom size, a light or dark color scheme, optionally a full-page capture, and optionally a query like "?state=error" so one file can show several states. You also receive the images, so check them before you describe them, and tell the user they are mockups, not the running app.

file.description: Path to the .html mockup, relative to the project root.

variants.description: What to render, at most 6; defaults to one desktop, light render.

preset.description: Viewport preset: desktop 1280×800, tablet 768×1024, mobile 390×844. Defaults to desktop.

label.description: Short name shown under the image, e.g. "Empty state, dark".

width.description: Custom viewport width in CSS pixels (200 to 2560).

height.description: Custom viewport height in CSS pixels (200 to 2000).

fullPage.description: Capture the whole page height (up to 6000px).

query.description: Appended to the file URL, starting with ? or #, e.g. "?state=empty".

fullPage.description: Default for every variant: capture the whole page height.

name: pr_sweep
description:
Plan and track a multi-PR sweep: a board like todo_write, specialized for working a batch of pull requests. Pass the full list of items every time (it replaces the previous one); keep exactly one item "in_progress" and advance each item's status as you go. This tool only records state and has no side effects; you do the real work with the other tools.

Two modes:
- "author": turn each task into its own PR. For each item: create a branch (e.g. `git worktree add` or `git checkout -b` via run_shell), make the change, commit, push the branch (`git push -u origin <branch>`), then gh_pr_create. Status flow: pending → in_progress → pushed → pr_open → done (or failed). Record the branch and the PR url as you get them.
- "process": work a list of existing open PRs (find them with gh_pr_list). For each item: gh_pr_checkout the PR, review/fix it (run_shell/review_changes), commit, push, gh_pr_comment if needed, then mark done. Record the PR reference.

Work items one at a time, update this board after each meaningful step, and put a short note on anything that fails or needs the user.

mode.description: "author" to create new PRs from tasks; "process" to work existing PRs.

items.description: The full sweep board, replacing any previous one.

task.description: What this item is: the task to author, or the existing PR to process.

branch.description: The branch worked on (author) or the PR head branch (process).

pr.description: PR reference once known: a number, "#123", or a URL.

note.description: Short note: a blocker, what was done, or why it failed.

name: recall_history
description: Page back into the earlier conversation after older turns have been compacted or their large tool outputs elided from your context. This reads your own full, un-summarized message log (read-only, no side effects). Filter by a substring `query` (case-insensitive; matches message text and tool-call arguments) and/or a message-index range (`from`/`to`, 0-based, as shown in the `#N` labels of a prior recall). Returns the matching earlier messages as compact labeled lines. Use it to recover a detail (a path, a value, an earlier decision) you no longer see rather than re-reading files or re-running commands. Output is size-capped; narrow the query or range if you need more of a specific message.

query.description: Case-insensitive substring to match against message text and tool-call arguments.

from.description: First message index to include (0-based, inclusive). Omit to start at the beginning.

to.description: Last message index to include (0-based, inclusive). Omit to read to the end.

limit.description: Maximum number of matching messages to return (most recent matches win). Default 30.

name: dispatch_writable_agent
description: Delegate a self-contained task to a subagent that can edit files and run shell commands in its own fresh context, then returns a written report. Edits and commands are confined to the project, and its shell commands have no network; it can also fetch public URLs and search the web, with each network request asking the user for approval first. Approving this call grants the subagent write access for the whole delegated task (edits and sandboxed commands do not prompt again per action), so scope the task clearly; on a host without an OS sandbox (e.g. Windows), each shell command it runs also asks the user for approval first. Use it to hand off an implementation, refactor, or fix you want done end to end (e.g. "add pagination to the users endpoint and update its tests"). For read-only investigation, use dispatch_agent instead.

description.description: A short label for the task (a few words).

prompt.description: The full task for the subagent, with all the context and acceptance criteria it needs.

agent.description: Optional: the name of a custom agent (from .houston/agents, marked `write: true`) to use. Omit for the default writable agent.

model.description: Optional: run the subagent on a different model from the current provider. Must be one of the provider's configured model ids; omit to use the current model.

resume.description: Optional: the id of a writable subagent from an earlier dispatch in this chat (shown at the end of its report). Continues that agent, and `prompt` becomes your follow-up message to it. Ids last for the app session.

name: spawn_session
description: Spawn a separate chat, seeded with a task you hand it, and start it running autonomously in the background. It appears in the sidebar with a live status; the user can open it to watch, answer an approval, or take over. Unlike dispatch_agent (an ephemeral read-only subagent that reports back into this turn), a spawned session is a persistent, independent conversation with its own context that keeps running after this turn ends. Use it only when the user asked for parallel or background work; to suggest parallel work yourself, use propose_session instead. The new session inherits your current approval policy (it is never more permissive), so its risky steps still pause for the user. By default it starts fresh with no view of this conversation, so put everything it needs in `prompt` (or pass context "fork").

prompt.description: The full task and context for the new session. It becomes the first message and is all the session sees, so include every detail it needs to work on its own.

title.description: Optional short title for the chat as it appears in the sidebar (a few words). Omit to derive one from the prompt.

worktree.description: Optional: run the session on a new git branch + worktree (an isolated checkout) so parallel sessions never collide. Omit to reuse the current workspace.

branch.description: New branch name to create and check out for the session.

base.description: Optional base ref to branch from. Defaults to the current HEAD, or to the remote default branch (e.g. origin/main) when HEAD is behind it with no commits of its own or has unrelated history.

context.description: Optional: "fresh" (the default) starts the session with only your prompt; "fork" also gives it a copy of this conversation so far, so it knows what was read, decided, and tried. Prefer "fork" when the task builds on this conversation, and "fresh" for self-contained work.

name: propose_session
description: Propose a separate session for a piece of work you noticed that could run in parallel with this one (independent of what you are doing here, and worth its own conversation). The user sees a card with Start session, Do it here, and Dismiss; nothing runs unless they choose. If they start it, it becomes its own background chat with this prompt, on its own git worktree when the project is a git repository, under the user's current approval policy, and reports back here when it finishes. Use it for real follow-ups, not one-line tweaks or speculation, and at most a few times per turn. Do not do the proposed work yourself unless the user asks for it here. Prefer this over spawn_session unless the user asked you to start parallel work.

title.description: Short title for the card and the new chat (a few words, under 60 characters).

prompt.description: The full brief for the new session: the task, the files or area, and what done looks like. It becomes the session's first message, so make it self-contained (or pass context "fork").

worktree.description: Optional: run the session on a new git branch + worktree (an isolated checkout) so parallel sessions never collide. Omit to reuse the current workspace.

branch.description: New branch name to create and check out for the session.

base.description: Optional base ref to branch from. Defaults to the current HEAD, or to the remote default branch (e.g. origin/main) when HEAD is behind it with no commits of its own or has unrelated history.

context.description: Optional: "fresh" (the default) starts the session with only your prompt; "fork" also gives it a copy of this conversation so far, so it knows what was read, decided, and tried. Prefer "fork" when the task builds on this conversation, and "fresh" for self-contained work.

name: schedule_run
description: Schedule a recurring (or one-time) background agent run. At each occurrence, a fresh session is started with the stored prompt; it appears alongside the other chats and runs autonomously under your current approval policy (never more permissive). Use it for routine, self-contained jobs the user wants repeated, e.g. "daily at 09:00, run the test suite and summarize any failures". The fired session sees only the stored prompt, so make it self-contained. Schedules fire while Houston is running (this is an in-app scheduler, not OS cron) and persist across restarts; an occurrence missed while Houston was closed fires once at the next launch.

name.description: A short human name (a few words); becomes each fired session's title.

spec.description: When to run: "every <N>m|h|d" (minimum 5 minutes), "daily at HH:MM", "weekdays at HH:MM", "weekly on <day> at HH:MM", or "once at YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM". Times are local, 24-hour.

prompt.description: The full task each fired run starts with. Self-contained: the fired session sees nothing from this chat.

name: list_scheduled_runs
description: List the scheduled background runs configured on this machine: id, name, recurrence, next/last fire time, and whether the last fire succeeded.

name: cancel_scheduled_run
description: Cancel a scheduled background run by id (from list_scheduled_runs or the schedule_run confirmation). Already-started sessions are unaffected; the schedule simply stops firing.

name: review_changes
description: Run an adversarial, multi-agent review of the current uncommitted changes for correctness, security, and quality. It spawns an independent read-only reviewer per dimension (each in its own fresh context, so they don't inherit your blind spots), then a skeptical verifier that re-checks every candidate finding against the real code and drops false positives, and returns the confirmed findings. Use it to self-review after completing a substantial change, before telling the user you are done, then fix what it confirms and verify the fixes directly. One review plus targeted fixes is usually enough: re-run it only if you make further substantial changes, and pass paths to scope the re-review to what changed rather than re-reviewing the whole diff. Reviews uncommitted changes (vs HEAD) by default; pass base to review against another commit or branch, and paths to limit the review to specific files.

base.description: Optional git ref to diff against (e.g. "main" or a commit SHA). Default: HEAD (all uncommitted changes).

paths.description: Optional: limit the review to these project-relative paths/directories (e.g. ["src/api"]). Default: the whole diff.

effort.description: Verification depth. 'high' verifies each finding with several independent skeptics and keeps only the majority-confirmed ones (more thorough, more model calls); 'normal' uses a single verifier. Default 'normal'; use 'high' for security-sensitive or high-stakes changes.

model.description: Optional: run the reviewer and verifier subagents on a different model from the current provider (e.g. a cheaper sibling for a routine review). Must be one of the provider's configured model ids; omit to use the current model.

name: gh_pr_create
description: Open a GitHub pull request for the current branch using the gh CLI. The branch must already be pushed to the remote (push it first with run_shell, e.g. `git push -u origin <branch>`). Requires approval (network) and is refused in plan mode. Returns the new PR URL.

body.description: PR description (Markdown). Omit for an empty body.

base.description: Base branch to merge into (e.g. "main"). Defaults to the repo default branch.

head.description: Head branch the PR is opened from. Defaults to the current branch.

draft.description: Open as a draft PR (default false).

name: gh_pr_list
description: List pull requests in the current repository via the gh CLI. Returns "#<number> [state] by <author> <url>" per PR, then each PR's title and head branch inside an untrusted-content fence. Requires approval (network).

author.description: Filter by author login (e.g. "@me" for yours).

name: gh_pr_view
description: View a pull request's details (title, state, author, body, file stats) via the gh CLI. Omit number to view the PR for the current branch. Set diff:true to also include the unified diff. Read-only, but requires approval (network).

number.description: PR number. Omit to use the current branch's PR.

diff.description: Also include the PR diff (default false).

name: gh_pr_comment
description: Post a comment on a GitHub pull request via the gh CLI. Omit number to comment on the current branch's PR. Requires approval (network) and is refused in plan mode.

number.description: PR number. Omit to use the current branch's PR.

name: gh_pr_checkout
description: Check out a GitHub pull request branch locally via the gh CLI (fetches the branch and switches the working tree to it). Use it to review or update an existing PR. Requires approval (network) and is refused in plan mode. Note: this switches the current checkout, so commit or stash your work first.

number.description: The PR number to check out.

name: gh_pr_checks
description: Show the CI check (status) rollup for a pull request via the gh CLI. Omit number to use the current branch's PR. Returns the rollup and "[<status>] check <n> <link>" per check, then the check and workflow names inside an untrusted-content fence keyed by n. Use it to see whether CI passed before relying on a PR. Read-only, but requires approval (network).

number.description: PR number. Omit to use the current branch's PR.

name: gh_pr_review
description: Submit a review on a GitHub pull request via the gh CLI: approve it, request changes, or leave a general review comment. Omit number to review the current branch's PR. A body is required for a comment or a change request (it is optional when approving). Posts publicly to the PR, so it requires approval (network) and is refused in plan mode.

number.description: PR number. Omit to use the current branch's PR.

action.description: The review verdict: approve, request_changes, or comment (default comment).

body.description: The review body (Markdown). Required for comment and request_changes; optional for approve.

name: gh_pr_merge
description: Merge an open GitHub pull request via the gh CLI. Omit number to merge the current branch's PR. Choose the merge method (a merge commit, squash, or rebase; default merge) and optionally delete the head branch afterward. This lands the change on the base branch, an outward and hard-to-undo action, so it requires approval (network) and is refused in plan mode.

number.description: PR number. Omit to use the current branch's PR.

method.description: How to merge: a merge commit, squash, or rebase (default merge).

delete_branch.description: Delete the head branch after a successful merge (default false).

subject.description: Commit subject for the merge/squash commit (optional; ignored for rebase).

body.description: Commit body for the merge/squash commit (optional; ignored for rebase).

name: gh_pr_set_state
description: Change a GitHub pull request's state via the gh CLI: close it (optionally deleting its branch), reopen it, mark a draft ready for review, or convert it back to a draft. close and reopen need the PR number; ready and draft use the current branch's PR when number is omitted. To land a PR use gh_pr_merge instead. Visible to everyone on the PR, so it requires approval (network) and is refused in plan mode.

number.description: PR number. Required for close and reopen; omit for ready or draft to use the current branch's PR.

action.description: close, reopen, ready (mark ready for review), or draft (convert to draft).

comment.description: A comment to post with the change (Markdown). Only for close and reopen.

delete_branch.description: When closing, also delete the head branch, locally and on the remote (default false).

name: gh_repo_create
description: Create a new GitHub repository via the gh CLI. By default it creates a private repo from the current project directory (adds it as the "origin" remote) and pushes the existing commits, so commit your work first (the directory must be a git repo with at least one commit; run `git init && git add -A && git commit` via run_shell if needed). Set source:false to instead create an empty remote repo with no local wiring. Requires approval (network) and is refused in plan mode. Returns the new repository URL.

name.description: Repository name, or "owner/name" to create under an org/user you can access.

source.description: Create from the current project directory and add it as the "origin" remote (default true). The directory must be a git repo with at least one commit.

push.description: Push the existing local commits to the new repo after creating it (default true; requires source).

clone.description: Clone the new (empty) repo into the project directory (default false; only when source is false).

name: gh_issue_list
description: List issues in the current repository via the gh CLI. Returns "#<number> [state] by <author> <url>" per issue, then each issue's title and labels inside an untrusted-content fence. Requires approval (network).

author.description: Filter by author login (e.g. "@me" for yours).

name: gh_issue_view
description: View a GitHub issue (title, state, author, labels, body) via the gh CLI. Set comments:true to include the comment thread. Issue and comment text arrives inside untrusted-content fences, since anyone who can open or comment on an issue wrote it. Read-only, but requires approval (network).

comments.description: Also include the comment thread (default false).

name: gh_issue_create
description: Open a new GitHub issue via the gh CLI. Requires approval (network) and is refused in plan mode. Returns the new issue URL.

body.description: Issue body (Markdown). Omit for an empty body.

label.description: Comma-separated labels to apply (each must already exist in the repo).

name: gh_issue_comment
description: Post a comment on a GitHub issue via the gh CLI. Requires approval (network) and is refused in plan mode.

name: gh_issue_set_state
description: Close or reopen a GitHub issue via the gh CLI. When closing, optionally give a reason (completed, not_planned, or duplicate) and, for a duplicate, the issue it duplicates. Visible to everyone on the issue, so it requires approval (network) and is refused in plan mode.

reason.description: Why it is being closed: completed, not_planned, or duplicate. Only for close; GitHub defaults to completed.

duplicate_of.description: When closing as a duplicate, the number of the issue this one duplicates.

comment.description: A comment to post with the change (Markdown).

name: gh_run_list
description: List recent GitHub Actions workflow runs in the repo via the gh CLI. Returns "<run-id> [status] (<event>)" per run, then each run's workflow, title, and branch inside an untrusted-content fence keyed by run id. Use a run-id with gh_run_view to inspect it. Requires approval (network).

workflow.description: Filter by workflow name or file (e.g. "ci.yml").

status.description: Filter by run status or conclusion.

name: gh_run_view
description: View a GitHub Actions workflow run via the gh CLI. Returns the run's id, outcome, URL, and each job's id, outcome, and failed step numbers, then the workflow, title, branch, and job and step names inside an untrusted-content fence. Set log_failed:true to print the logs of only the failed steps instead, fenced (the fastest way to diagnose a CI failure). Get run ids from gh_run_list. Read-only, but requires approval (network).

log_failed.description: Print the logs of the failed steps instead of the run summary (default false).
